page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-64GB is a Cloud Native server instance configured with 32 shared AMD EPYC 7542 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features 32 physical cores with single-thread execution per core, alongside a cache hierarchy consisting of 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. It includes hardware-level support for AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instructions. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates average multi-core processing and memory capabilities, alongside some notable performance variations. While single-core performance under stress-ng is positioned in the bottom 10%, multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench scores fall within the middle 50% tier. The instance exhibits strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU encryption capabilities, both scoring in the top 25%. Conversely, large-model LLM inference prompt processing for a 70B model is weak, landing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth and static web serving throughput consistently register in the average range.

Given the shared CPU allocation, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that can tolerate shared resource contention. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for parallel processing tasks, multi-threaded decompression, and moderate web serving. However, the lack of dedicated CPU cores and local storage makes it less suitable for sustained high-performance single-core operations or I/O-heavy database workloads. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded data processing, batch compilation, and distributed web serving.
